challenges.title: Serve Receive Formation
challenges.description: The other team is about to serve, so your team needs to get into serve receive formation. Your goal is to position players so the serve can be passed cleanly to the setter. Three players should spread out in the back row to cover the court and receive the serve, while the setter stays near the net ready for the second touch.
challenges.hint: Serve receive is how your team lines up to pass the other team's serve. In a W formation, three back-row players spread out to pass the serve: one left back, one middle back, and one right back. The libero is usually the strongest passer, so try placing them in the center back. The setter should stay near the net so they can set the next ball.
challenges.success_message: Perfect W formation! Your passers cover the whole back court and your setter is ready to set.
challenges.learn_tip: In serve receive, the goal is to get the first touch under control. The back row spreads out to cover as much court as possible, while the setter stays near the net ready for the second touch.

challenges.title: Spiking Attack
challenges.description: Your team has the ball and the setter just set it high on the left side. Arrange your players — blockers jump at the net, hitters approach, and back row covers tips.
challenges.hint: Two blockers at the net defend. The outside hitter approaches from the left. Back row players cover the court.
challenges.success_message: Textbook attack formation! Blockers up, hitter approaching, back row ready to cover the tip.
challenges.learn_tip: When your team attacks, back row players 'cover' the hitter — ready to dig if the block sends it back.

challenges.title: Defensive Block
challenges.description: The other team's outside hitter is about to spike from the left side. Get your team into defensive position — two blockers at the net and back row in defensive spots.
challenges.hint: Two players jump at the net to block. The other four drop back in a defensive base formation.
challenges.success_message: Great defensive setup! Two blockers seal the net and back row is spread to cover the whole court.
challenges.learn_tip: The libero almost always plays center back — they're your best passer and get the most digs from that spot.

challenges.title: Free Ball Reception
challenges.description: The opponent can't attack — they're sending a soft free ball over the net. This is your team's chance to transition into a full offensive formation. Unlike serve receive, everyone is already moving, so your front-row hitters need to spread wide and prepare to attack while back-row players get into passing position.
challenges.hint: A free ball means easy pass — so use it to set up a great attack. The setter runs to the net right-of-center. Both outside hitters spread wide on their approach sides. The libero takes the pass from center-back, and the middle blocker swings off the net to approach for a quick set.
challenges.success_message: Perfect free-ball transition! Hitters are in approach position and the setter is ready for the pass.
challenges.learn_tip: Free balls are gold — the other team just handed you an easy pass. Use it to run your best offensive play, not just keep the ball alive.

challenges.title: Setter Transition
challenges.description: Your libero just dug a hard spike from the back row. Now your team needs to transition from defense to offense — fast. The setter has to sprint from wherever they were digging to their setting position near the net, while hitters peel off and start their approaches. Get everyone into attack mode.
challenges.hint: After a dig, the setter's first priority is to sprint to the net (right-of-center). The outside hitter swings out wide-left for their approach. The middle blocker pivots from the net and steps back to approach. The libero who just dug stays ready for cover. Back-row players hold their defensive lanes in case the ball comes back.
challenges.success_message: Smooth transition! The setter is running the offense and hitters are loaded for the attack.
challenges.learn_tip: Transition is the hardest skill in volleyball — going from digging a spike to attacking in under two seconds. The setter's speed to the net is the most important factor.
